meta.title: Operation of Water Bath in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To provide controlled temperature heating for pharmacognosy experiments including phytochemical tests, extraction procedures, and evaporation of solvents from plant extracts.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for all procedures requiring controlled temperature water heating from room temperature to 100°C.
procedure: Fill the water bath with distilled water up to the recommended fill level (typically 2/3 full).
Switch on the water bath and set the thermostat to the required temperature.
Allow the water to reach and equilibrate at the set temperature before inserting samples.
Verify temperature using a calibrated laboratory thermometer placed in the bath.
Place beakers, flasks, or test tubes in the water bath — use appropriate bath rings or wire gauze to prevent tipping.
Ensure the submerged level of the sample vessel's contents is at or below the water bath level for effective heat transfer.
For evaporation of extracts: place round-bottom flasks on the bath surface and allow gentle warming to evaporate solvent.
Monitor the temperature at regular intervals and adjust the thermostat to maintain the set temperature.
Replenish water lost by evaporation with warm distilled water to maintain the fill level.
After use, switch off the water bath.
For extended storage, drain, clean the tank with dilute disinfectant, and refill before next use.
Record temperature, duration, and purpose in the equipment logbook.
precautions: Never allow the water level to drop below the heating element — dry heating burns the element.
Use distilled water only — tap water causes limescale deposits on the heating element, reducing efficiency.
Do not heat sealed containers — pressure build-up can cause breakage or expulsion of contents.
Use tongs or heat-resistant gloves when removing hot vessels from the bath.
Keep electrical connections away from water — ensure the unit is properly earthed.
Do not heat volatile organic solvents in an open vessel on the water bath in a poorly ventilated area.
Calibrate the thermostat against a NIST-traceable thermometer regularly.
Clean the bath monthly — algal growth and mineral deposits degrade heating performance.
